answer: Agents earn transferable credit only after completing a randomly selected task whose result is checked against a hidden test set; each account’s credit is locked in a vault until its work passes. Splitting into sybils does not multiply credit, because tasks are assigned per unit of verified work, not per identity. An attacker must therefore pay the real compute and labor cost for each passing result, while the reef of independent checks makes cheap copied submissions fail. Velvet onboarding cannot bypass that cost.
